body: Flag: CLEAN. Infosys is the reference case for disclosure and minority treatment in Indian IT: founders/promoter group own only ~13%; no pledging; capital-allocation policy returns ~85% of free cash flow over 5 years via dividends and buybacks. Buybacks: 2017 (Rs 13,000 cr), 2019, 2021, 2022 and the Rs 18,000 cr tender at Rs 1,800/share approved 11-Sep-2025, in which the promoters chose not to participate (their stake rising slightly to ~13.4% as shares are extinguished). Governance episodes: (1) 2016-17 founder-board conflict over CEO Vishal Sikka, the Panaya acquisition and severance pay to ex-CFO Rajiv Bansal; Sikka resigned (Aug-2017); Nilekani returned as chairman; an external probe found no wrongdoing in Panaya. (2) Oct-2019 anonymous 'ethical employees' whistleblower letter alleged accounting manipulation by CEO Salil Parekh/CFO; the audit committee's independent probe (with law firm) found no evidence; the US SEC closed its inquiry (2020); stock fell ~16% in a day then recovered -- a whistleblower allegation not upheld. (3) SEBI settled insider-trading proceedings involving some employees (no promoter wrongdoing). Status Nov-2026: no open promoter governance issues; GST demand disputes are tax matters. Investor read: buyback decisions where promoters abstain are a strong signal of alignment.

data.good_conduct: 85% FCF return policy; buybacks; promoters skipped 2025 buyback
